lean.statement:
{J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0<h) :
    let t := fun i : Fin J => h/2*(1-Real.cos ((i : ℝ)/(J-1 : ℝ)*Real.pi))
    let ell := fun j : Fin J => Lagrange.basis univ t j
    ∀ j, 0 ≤ ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..h, (ell j).eval s
approved_definition_context: J is a natural number. Fin J is the finite type of zero-based integer indices0,...,J-1. Its coercion to the real numbers is exact; (J-1:R) in the displayed formula is real subtraction after casting J.

Lagrange.basis univ t j is the actual real cardinal polynomial obtained as the product over all i different from j of (X-t_i)/(t_j-t_i). Its eval s is polynomial evaluation at real s. No cardinal formula or positive coefficient premise is assumed.

The notation integral s in0..h is the oriented interval integral against ordinary real Lebesgue measure, not a probability law or a trigonometric weighted measure. Under h>0 it is the usual integral over the finite interval. Polynomial continuity supplies integrability internally.

Real.cos is the ordinary real cosine; Real.pi is pi. h is a real scalar. Both endpoint indices are quantified. The statement supplies no logarithmic interpolation bound, Hessian, gradient, probability kernel, query-cost or integrator assumption.
